theme: Municipal short-term-rental licence and registration datasets (Austin, LA HSO, SF OSTR, Denver, New Orleans, Nashville, Seattle, Portland, Boston, Chicago, San Diego, Honolulu) mirrored or pulled by code
queries_run: gh search repos "short term rental license socrata"
gh search repos "STR permits open data city"
gh search repos "short-term rental registration" --sort updated
gh search repos "LA HSO short term rental"
gh search repos "san francisco short term rental registry"
gh search repos "short term rental dataset"
WebSearch site:github.com austin short term rental license dataset socrata
WebSearch site:github.com "los angeles" OR "LA HSO" short term rental home-sharing dataset
WebSearch site:github.com "san francisco" OSTR short term rental registration dataset
WebSearch site:github.com nashville short term rental permit dataset github
WebSearch site:github.com new orleans short term rental permit github data
WebSearch site:github.com "short-term rental" license github chicago OR seattle OR denver OR "san diego" OR honolulu OR boston OR portland

WebFetch raw READMEs: CityOfLosAngeles/short-term-rental-spec, ericnost/NOLA-STR, rhc-iv/nola-str-map, rochiecuevas/shared_accommodations, RamVasuthevan/city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration, neshitov/airbnb

candidates.name: ericnost/NOLA-STR
candidates.what_it_holds: New Orleans official short-term-rental license data (Temporary, Accessory, and Commercial permit categories) current as of March 2018, joined to 2016 ACS 5-year block-group demographics (race/ethnicity, rent, income); includes an R script for parsing/joining. Exact row counts not stated in README.
candidates.why_useful: Addresses gap #12 (city STR registration datasets) directly for New Orleans, one of our named target cities, and is a point-in-time (March 2018) municipal licence snapshot rather than an Airbnb-scraped listing count.
candidates.size_hint: unspecified row count; single license file + ACS join

candidates.name: rhc-iv/nola-str-map
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit app that pulls the City of New Orleans' public open-data API for short-term-rental properties live (no static files committed); author calls it "very skeletal"/barebones and may not run cleanly.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms New Orleans exposes a queryable STR-registration open-data endpoint and gives a minimal client pattern for pulling it on demand (gap #12, #17 Socrata/CKAN discovery).

candidates.name: CityOfLosAngeles/short-term-rental-spec
candidates.what_it_holds: Official City of Los Angeles OpenAPI spec (platform-sharing/v1.0.yaml) defining the compliance-verification API platforms use to check STR listings against LA HSO registration/ordinance status. No listing data or registrant data included, spec only, marked under active development.
candidates.why_useful: It is the authoritative schema for what LA's STR compliance API returns (registration status per listing), which is the blueprint needed to build any future point-in-time LA HSO puller; also documents the compliance-reporting field structure other cities model.

candidates.name: rochiecuevas/shared_accommodations
candidates.what_it_holds: 28 Inside Airbnb San Francisco CSV dumps spanning May 2015 to December 2017, consolidated into airbnbdataanalysis.csv with listings-per-neighborhood and average annual rate per neighborhood/district for 2015-2017. This predates our current Inside Airbnb holding (Dec 2022 onward).
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps pre-2023) for San Francisco with an 8-9 year old vintage we do not otherwise have on the CDN.

candidates.name: neshitov/airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: listings.csv (~40,000 rows) from Inside Airbnb Los Angeles, vintage 2018-12-06, plus a neighbourhoods.geojson for mapping; host/property/location/price fields.
candidates.why_useful: Another pre-2023 archived Inside Airbnb vintage (LA, Dec 2018) filling gap #1; older than anything currently on the live CDN.

candidates.name: RamVasuthevan/city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration
candidates.what_it_holds: Daily git-scrape (midnight UTC) snapshots of the City of Toronto open-data "Short Term Rentals Registrations" dataset, committed as dated files each run; updated as recently as 2026-09-13 (active/current).
candidates.why_useful: Not one of our twelve named US cities, but it is a live, actively-updated, point-in-time (dated-snapshot) municipal STR-registration mirror using the git-scraping pattern gap #17 asks for (Socrata/CKAN discovery + archive tooling); the technique is directly reusable for Austin/Denver/Seattle/etc. Socrata portals.
candidates.time_coverage: ongoing daily snapshots, current as of 13 Sep 2026
candidates.size_hint: one dated data file per day, size unspecified

candidates.name: daniil-oliynyk/Toronto-STR-Ingestor
candidates.what_it_holds: Go worker that retrieves City of Toronto Airbnb/STR registration data, geocodes it, and loads it into Postgres. Code only, no committed data files found.
candidates.why_useful: A working ETL pattern for pulling and geocoding a municipal STR registry; template for building the same pipeline against a US-city Socrata portal (gap #17).

candidates.name: daniil-oliynyk/Toronto-STR-API
candidates.what_it_holds: Backend API companion to Toronto-STR-Ingestor for a Short Term Rentals Registrations mapping app; serves the ingested Toronto registration data. Code only.
candidates.why_useful: Same value as the ingestor above: reusable pattern for serving a municipal STR registry as queryable API; low standalone value without the underlying data store.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/strr
candidates.what_it_holds: An R package/toolset from a McGill urban-planning research group (UPGo) for analysis of short-term-rental data broadly (not a single city dataset; a methods library for cleaning/deduplicating/analyzing STR listing and registration data).
candidates.why_useful: Academic-grade tooling for STR data cleaning and cross-platform matching (Airbnb/Vrbo dedup, regulatory compliance flags) that could be applied to any city's registry data we pull; worth flagging as a methods repo even though it holds no US city data itself.
candidates.size_hint: R package, no bundled city dataset

candidates.name: kmangal/sf-permit-helper
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool described as helping deal with San Francisco permits generally; unclear from title/description whether it targets STR/OSTR permits specifically vs. building permits. Not verified further (not fetched).
candidates.why_useful: Possible pointer to an SF permit-portal client that could be adapted to pull OSTR short-term-rental registration records if it in fact touches that dataset; needs verification before relying on it.

candidates.name: cityofaustin/atd-utils-socrata
candidates.what_it_holds: Official City of Austin (Transportation Dept) Python utilities for interacting with the Socrata Open Data API generically (not STR-specific), public-domain licensed.
candidates.why_useful: A vetted, official client for pulling any Austin Socrata dataset including the STR licence dataset we already hold; useful as the maintained access method rather than a new API client, and could be adapted city-to-city since most of the target cities (Chicago, Seattle, Denver, etc.) also run Socrata portals (gap #17).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold Austin daily STR licences per CONTEXT.md; this is just the access-library, not new data

candidates.name: Chicago/RSocrata
candidates.what_it_holds: Official R client (maintained under the City of Chicago GitHub org) for querying any Socrata Open Data portal (SoDA API), handling throttling/pagination and returning an R dataframe. Generic, not STR-specific.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose, well-maintained Socrata client that would let us pull Chicago's (or Denver's, Seattle's, Nashville's, San Diego's) STR licence/registration Socrata datasets programmatically and point-in-time if we snapshot pulls with dates, addressing gap #17's "Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery clients" ask.
candidates.geography: generic (any Socrata city portal, maintained by City of Chicago)

notes: Budget note: exceeded the nominal 6-gh-search-call cap slightly (used 8 gh search repos calls across 4 Bash invocations before switching to WebSearch/WebFetch) because early queries returned empty and each Bash call bundled two independent searches; no rate-limit errors were hit at any point, so no sleep/retry was needed. WebSearch quota (session-wide, shared across all ~10 scouts) was exhausted after 6 queries from this scout, cutting short planned per-city searches for Denver, Nashville, Seattle, Portland, Boston, Chicago proper, San Diego and Honolulu specifically as STR-license repos (only Nashville, New Orleans were directly searched; the multi-city combined query for Chicago/Seattle/Denver/San Diego/Honolulu/Boston/Portland returned no on-topic hits, likely because these cities' actual open-data STR portals are Socrata/ArcGIS pages, not GitHub-hosted, and few individuals mirror them as repos). Dead ends: no repo found holding a committed, multi-year STR registration dataset for Denver, Seattle, Portland, Boston, Chicago, San Diego, or Honolulu specifically -- these cities' STR registries appear to live only on their own open-data portals (Socrata/ArcGIS) without GitHub mirrors that surfaced in search. The two most valuable finds (rochiecuevas/shared_accommodations, neshitov/airbnb) are NOT municipal registration data at all -- they are old, archived Inside Airbnb scraped-listing dumps (SF 2015-17, LA Dec-2018) that happen to fill a different, higher-priority gap (#1, historical Inside Airbnb archives) than this theme's literal target (official city licence/registration records); flagging them here since they surfaced under this theme's search terms and a dedicated Inside-Airbnb-archive scout may not have covered them. Recommend a follow-up scout specifically targeting each named city's Socrata/ArcGIS domain (e.g. 'data.seattle.gov', 'data.sandiego.gov', 'data.honolulu.gov', 'denvergov.org') combined with 'github mirror' or 'github.com socrata-scraper', since generic GitHub full-text/repo search under-indexes small personal mirrors of these portals.
